open_points.subject: K-02 function purity, TrialExecution outcome, and admission
open_points.text: “no clock, no randomness” conflicts with “guards against depending on the time or on chance by accident; it is no guarantee against code written to get around it”
open_points.question: Are clock and randomness forbidden invariants whose use or attempted circumvention makes an execution a sandbox violation and prevents admission, or are only calls through guarded standard-library entry points forbidden, so an implementation that obtains time or randomness another way may succeed and be admitted?
options: Any clock or randomness access is prohibited; detected access or circumvention yields `sandbox_violation`, although prevention may be incomplete.
The enforced product rule covers only the standard-library entry points; access obtained by another route may execute successfully and contribute to an `admitted` verdict.
open_points.default_guess: Treat the prohibition as normative but implement only the stated best-effort guards; a successful undetected workaround can therefore pass and be admitted.

witness.initial: A contract version has a nonempty passing trial corpus and no active implementation.
events: An authoring agent submits Python code that avoids the guarded standard-library entry points but obtains a changing time or random value by another route.
The kernel runs the corpus for admission.
outcomes: The sandbox classifies the circumvention as `sandbox_violation`; admission is `refused`, and no activation is created.
The execution succeeds because only the standard-library entry points are guarded; if its outputs satisfy the cases, admission is `admitted` and the kernel activates it.
witness.observer: The submitting agent sees different trial evidence, admission verdict, and activation state; later run starters see whether the contract version has a current activation.
